title: Vintage Fender Jazzmaster Value Guide: Eras And Color
description: Compare vintage Fender Jazzmaster value by era, original finish, pickups and condition. Joe explains custom colors, changed parts and appraisal details.
alt: Sunburst Fender Jazzmaster with a gold pickguard, white pickup covers and a vibrato arm

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Fender Jazzmaster Worth?
faqs.a: A played, largely original sunburst 1965 Fender Jazzmaster with its original case falls around $6,000 to $7,000 in the completed-sale comparisons reviewed as of October 2026. I use that range for guitars retaining their original finish, pickups and main hardware, with ordinary wear and limited reversible changes.

faqs.q: What Condition Does This Price Range Assume?
faqs.a: Original finish, pickups, electronics and principal hardware, with original case and ordinary playing wear. Quality refret accepted; removable strap locks with original buttons retained included. Not a museum-quality band. I match those details before using the $6,000 to $7,000 range for an individual guitar.

faqs.q: Is A Dealer Offer The Same As The Published Range?
faqs.a: It isn't. The table describes completed-sale comparisons before shipping and tax. A buying offer also accounts for the instrument's condition, selling costs, preparation and the dealer's margin. I explain an offer for the actual guitar rather than promising the top of a general range.

faqs.q: Does A Quality Refret Change The Collector Category?
faqs.a: A quality refret is accepted maintenance and preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise all-original guitar. It takes the instrument out of the museum-quality category. Neck reshaping is a separate alteration.
